plant-001.description: Hibiscus is a tropical flowering shrub known for its large, colourful blooms. It attracts pollinators and adds a bright splash of colour to gardens.

care.water: Keep soil evenly moist; avoid waterlogging

plant-001.bloomTime: Often flowers through warm months; timing depends on local climate and care.
plant-001.funFact: Hibiscus flowers are visited by butterflies and other pollinators.

plant-002.description: Aloe vera is a hardy succulent with thick, water-storing leaves. It is well suited to sunny spots and needs less frequent watering than many garden plants.

care.water: Allow soil to dry between watering

plant-002.bloomTime: Mature plants may send up flower spikes in warm conditions.
plant-002.funFact: Its fleshy leaves store water, helping the plant tolerate dry periods.

plant-003.description: Tulsi is a fragrant herb widely grown in South Asia. Its aromatic leaves and small flowers make it a familiar feature in home and community gardens.

care.water: Water when the top soil begins to dry

plant-003.bloomTime: Small flower spikes commonly appear in warm weather.
plant-003.funFact: Tulsi belongs to the mint family, Lamiaceae.

plant-004.description: The areca palm is a graceful, clump-forming palm with arching, feather-like fronds. It is commonly used to bring a lush tropical look to landscaped spaces.

care.sun: Bright filtered light or partial shade
care.water: Water when the top layer starts to dry
care.soil: Rich, well-draining potting or garden soil

plant-004.bloomTime: Mature outdoor palms can flower in warm conditions.
plant-004.funFact: Its many slender stems create a soft, fountain-like shape.

plant-005.description: Marigolds produce cheerful yellow and orange flower heads and are popular in ornamental gardens. They grow quickly in warm weather with good sunlight.

care.water: Water at the base when the soil starts to dry

plant-005.bloomTime: Often blooms from a few weeks after planting until weather becomes unsuitable.
plant-005.funFact: Marigolds are frequently planted in mixed gardens to add colour and attract beneficial insects.
